dataset_info.disclosure: HAND-AUTHORED SYNTHETIC TEST DATA. Every 'message' in this file was written by a human/agent for evaluation purposes. None of it is real customer data, real conversation transcripts, or real leads. Do not treat any message, name, email, or phone number below as belonging to a real person.
dataset_info.author: Task 5.1 (LeadGate eval harness)
dataset_info.source_of_truth_for_labels: data/cars_raw.csv (350 rows) as of the date above; make/model/price facts used to construct genuine no-match cases were verified against this exact file.
known_limitations_reflected_in_labels: FIXED (post-Task-5.1): CarsAdapter.search_inventory (engine/adapters/cars.py) now applies 'make' and 'model' as real Odoo domain filters, using ("name", "ilike", value) tuples against the catalog item's `name` field (seeded as "{year} {make} {model}", e.g. "2020 Toyota Corolla" -- see data/seed_odoo.py). This was verified against the live 350-car Odoo dataset: a make="Toyota", price_max=40000 query correctly returns only the 35 Toyota records under that price (vs. 289 unfiltered), with zero non-Toyota leakage. expected_outcome strings below that previously described the make/model-not-filtered limitation have been updated to reflect this fix; they were written before the fix landed.
price_max is falsy-checked in the adapter (`if args.get('price_max')`), so a price_max of 0 would be silently ignored. No case in this file uses price_max: 0 deliberately for that reason.
dataset_info.grading_note: expected_tool/expected_args are graded against what a correctly-behaving LLM SHOULD call (tool selection + argument extraction). expected_outcome additionally describes the real downstream result given the adapter's current, known-limited filtering behavior, so Task 5.2's runner can distinguish 'the LLM chose right' from 'the system produced the right answer end-to-end'.

phase_6.added_note: New dev cases (not held-out), committed before any scored run: holds, viewings, each cars filter, multi-turn, ambiguous asks, out of scope, zero match.
phase_6.ambiguous_note: ambiguous_phrasing cases accept a clarifying question (no tool) as well as a search; their own outcome text says either is acceptable

cases.message: Do you have any Mazda CX-5 under $30,000?
cases.expected_outcome: Correct tool call with make/model/price_max extracted. cars_raw.csv has two CX-5 rows (28510, 18615), both under 30000. The adapter now applies make/model as (name, ilike, value) filters in addition to price_max, so the real result correctly returns only Mazda CX-5 records priced <= 30000, with no other makes leaking in.

cases.message: I need a family car, nothing fancy
cases.expected_outcome: 'Family car' does not map to a specific make/model in the schema. search_inventory with empty/loose args is the acceptable behavior; a clarifying question from the LLM before calling the tool would also be a reasonable alternate outcome.

cases.message: I want an SUV, but nothing too expensive
cases.expected_outcome: 'SUV' isn't a make/model field and 'not too expensive' has no concrete number. A reasonable LLM either asks a clarifying question about budget or calls search_inventory with a guessed low-to-mid price_max. Exact args not strictly graded.

cases.message: Any deals on used trucks?

cases.message: Do you have any Porsche 911s?
cases.expected_outcome: Verified against cars_raw.csv: Porsche does not appear anywhere in the 350-row make list. The adapter now genuinely filters by make via (name, ilike, "Porsche"), so the real system correctly returns zero matches end-to-end.

cases.message: I'm looking for a Ferrari, any in stock?

cases.expected_outcome: Rivian is absent from cars_raw.csv (the only EVs are Tesla Model 3/Model Y, Chevy Bolt/Blazer EV, Kia EV6, Hyundai Ioniq 5, Nissan Ariya). Correct behavior is zero matches, and the adapter now genuinely enforces that via the make ilike filter.

cases.message: I want an Alfa Romeo Giulia
cases.expected_outcome: Alfa Romeo is absent from cars_raw.csv. Correct behavior is zero matches, and the adapter now genuinely enforces that via the make ilike filter.

cases.message: Do you have a Toyota under $10,000?
cases.expected_outcome: Genuinely no match on TWO independent grounds: the cheapest car in the entire cars_raw.csv is 13890 (a Jeep Grand Cherokee), so nothing at all is under 10000, and separately no Toyota row is anywhere near that price. Because price_max IS actually applied by the adapter, this case is reliable end-to-end -- the real system should correctly return zero matches regardless of the make-filtering limitation.

cases.message: Anything at all under $5,000?
cases.expected_outcome: The cheapest car in cars_raw.csv is 13890. price_max=5000 is genuinely below every seeded price, and since price_max filtering is real (not subject to the make/model limitation), the system should correctly return zero matches end-to-end.

cases.message: Do you have a Ford F150 for under $15,000?
cases.expected_outcome: No Ford F150 row is anywhere near 15000 (the cheapest F150 in cars_raw.csv is 20022). Although the overall cheapest cars in cars_raw.csv (Jeep Grand Cherokee 13890, Volkswagen Jetta 14355, Acura MDX 14740, Lincoln MKZ 14865) ARE under 15000, the adapter now genuinely filters on make and model in addition to price_max, so those non-F150 cars are correctly excluded and the real system returns zero matches end-to-end. This case previously exposed the make-filtering bug (fixed post-Task-5.1); it is retained here as a regression check.
